This Writ Petition has been filed seeking direction to the Respondents Nos.1 and 5 to take criminal action against those who are responsible among the Employees of the Respondent No.6 (TASMAC) Retail Vending Shop, Pub, Club, TASMAC Bar and Private Bar, Hotel, Shop, Medical or any other individual third person for selling Alcohol,
Cigarette, Cool lip and any intoxicating liquor or any narcotic drug or tobacco products or psychotropic substance and other intoxicate substances to Minors including School Students under Section 77 and 78 of the Juvenile Justice (JJ) Act, 2015 and Section 188 Indian Penal Code 1860 and habitual offenders has to be detained under the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Forest Offenders, Sand Offenders, Slum- Grabbers and Video Pirates Act, 1982, (the Goondas Act).

sentences.text: The Petitioner had already filed W.P.(MD).No.2543 of 2019, wherein, almost an identical plea was taken by the Petitioner.

The relevant portion of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis submission made by the petitioner before the Court in the aforesaid Writ Petition is extracted as under:
4.4.

Along with the writ petition, the petitioner has also filed four miscellaneous petitions seeking interim injunction restraining the fifth respondent, its men and agents from selling any alcoholic breweries to those, who are below 21 years of age at their retail shops, pubs and bars situated inthe state of Tamil Nadu; and interim directions to the respondents 1 and 5 to display in Tamil all evils of consuming alcoholic beverages in all retail shops, pubs and bars of the fifth respondent situated in the state of Tamil Nadu for public view, to display in Tamil, the price list and all contact details of higher officials to submit complaint in case of over pricing, and issue receipts for payment for all alcoholic beverages in all retail shops, pubs and bars of the fifth respondent situated in the State of Tamil Nadu, and to ensure and print name, ingredients and quantity of ingredients of liquor, quality, purity, standard,
grade, trade name, brand name, price and address of manufacturer as per the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 on label of bottles of all alcoholic beverages in Tamil language, which are selling in retail shops, pubs and bars of the fifth respondent situated in the state of Tamil Nadu.
3. This Court has already considered the plea of the petitioner and passed an order on 04.01.2023,
which reads as under:
20.

Further, it may not be out of place to mention the report of the World Health Organisation, which states that reducing the harmful use of alcohol and its associated health and social burden is a public health priority and which deserves focus by the respective Central and State Governments.
Therefore, it is just and necessary that effective steps must be taken to reduce the menace of liquor consumption, in order to safeguard the public health and welfare.

Though this court is not oblivious that policy https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis decision of the Government cannot be interfered judicially, considering the larger public interest, the following directions /
suggestions are issued in these writ petitions:
(i) The central Government may take into consideration and give instructions to the State of Tamil Nadu and Director General of Police to impose a licensing regime for sale, purchase and usage of Indian Made Foreign Liquor.
(ii) The State Government shall give necessary instructions to the retail outlet shops through TASMAC that only the consumer, who has an alcohol license, can be permitted to buy Indian Made Foreign Liquor.
(iii) The labelling requirements under the Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulations, 2018 and the Food Safety and Standards (Packing and B.Ramkumar Adityan vs Additional Chief Secretary on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83068093/
3 Labeling) Regulations, 2011 shall be strictly complied with.

sentences.text: (iv) The state government shall also consider printing the labels, displaying price list and contact details for registering complaints in Tamil.
(v) The state government and TASMAC shall ensure the strict compliance of the regulations relating to management and administration of staff, etc.
(vi) The state Government shall ensure that liquor is not sold to persons below 21 years of age.
(vii) The state government and the TASMAC may consider reducing the business hours i.e., between 2.00 PM and 8.00 P.M. considering the public health and welfare.

4.Now, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the respondents have installed number of automatic liquor vending machines, as a result of which, even youngsters are free to purchase liquor and intoxicating materials including tobacco products.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5

. The learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents 1 to 5 submitted that the above submission of the petitioner is incorrect and only four automatic liquor vending machines have been installed and that too within the elite shops in Express Avenue Mall, Ten Square mall, VR mall and Phoenix mall and that vending is under the supervision of the Tasmac officials and in accordance with the provisions of the Tamil Nadu Liquor Retail Vending (In Shops and Bars) Rules,
2003.

sentences.text: He further submitted that a circular dated 19.09.2022 has also been issued to all the employees of Tasmac shops to strictly follow the rules.
6. Recording the above submission, the Writ Petition stands dismissed.
No costs.

Consequently,
connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
